title: Seasons and the Earth's Motions
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Seasons and the Earth's Motions Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The Earth rotates on its axis (day and night) and revolves around the Sun (a year). The tilt of the Earth's axis causes seasons in many places; the Philippines, near the equator, has a dry season and a wet season shaped by the monsoons (amihan and habagat). (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): rotation and revolution, day and night, the tilt of the Earth, and the dry and wet seasons in the Philippines. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rotation causes day and night; revolution takes a year.
key_sub: The Philippines has a dry season and a wet season.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth spins (rotates) on its axis once every 24 hours, which causes day and night. It moves (revolves) around the Sun once every 365 days. The Earth's axis is tilted, so different places get more direct sunlight at different times of the year.

The Philippines is near the equator, so it is warm all year. Instead of four seasons, it has a dry season (about December to May) and a wet season (about June to November). The habagat (southwest monsoon) brings rain; the amihan (northeast monsoon) brings cooler, drier air.

Example

What causes day and night?

Spinning

Answer: the Earth's rotation

Example

Which monsoon brings heavy rain in July?

Southwest

Answer: the habagat

Common mistakes

  • Thinking seasons happen because the Earth gets closer to the Sun.
  • Mixing up rotation and revolution.
  • Thinking the Philippines has four seasons like countries far from the equator.

faq.q: Why is it hot in April and May?
faq.a: The Sun is high in the sky and there is little rain.

faq.q: Why does the Sun rise in the east?
faq.a: The Earth rotates from west to east.

items.q: In which direction does the Sun appear to rise?
items.e: The Earth rotates from west to east.

items.q: Earth turns 360° in 24 hours. How many degrees does it turn in 6 hours?
What causes day and night?
c: the Moon moving around the Earth
the Earth revolving around the Sun
the Earth rotating on its axis
items.e: One rotation takes about 24 hours.

items.q: Stars seem to move about 15° across the sky each hour because Earth spins. Joy watches a star for 2 hours. About how many degrees does it move?
The Earth turns 15° every hour. How long does it take to turn 270°?
How long does the Earth take to revolve once around the Sun?
items.e: Revolution is the Earth's motion around the Sun.

items.q: Earth turns 360° in 24 hours. How many degrees does it turn in 18 hours?
Stars seem to move about 15° across the sky each hour because Earth spins. Kevin watches a star for 6 hours. About how many degrees does it move?
The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, which is 15° every hour. How far does it turn in 20 hours?
How long does the Moon take to go through all its phases?
items.e: The word month comes from Moon.

items.q: Which way does the Earth spin?
items.e: Day and night happen because the Earth spins; the Sun only seems to move.

items.q: The Earth turns 15° every hour. How long does it take to turn 75°?
Why are days and nights almost the same length all year in the Philippines?
c: places near the equator have about 12 hours of daylight all year
the Moon gives light at night
items.e: Day length changes much more near the poles.

items.q: What is rotation?
c: the movement of the Earth around the Sun
the movement of the Moon around the Earth
the spinning of the Earth on its axis
items.e: Rotation causes day and night.

items.q: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
c: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth.
Earth's shadow covers part of it every night.
items.e: These are the phases of the Moon.

items.q: What is revolution?
c: the movement of the Earth in its orbit around the Sun
the change from day to night
items.e: One revolution is one year.

items.q: What happens in a lunar eclipse?
c: Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
The Sun hides behind Earth's clouds.
items.e: The Moon can look red.

items.q: The Earth turns 15° every hour. How long does it take to turn 300°?
The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, which is 15° every hour. How far does it turn in 1 hour?
What causes ocean tides?
c: mainly the Moon's gravity pulling on Earth's water
items.e: Two high tides a day happen in most places.

items.e: 360 ÷ 6 = 60 newtons. The amount of matter is the same, but the Moon's weaker gravity pulls less.

items.q: What is a dwarf planet?
c: a round object that orbits the Sun but has not cleared its path, like Pluto
items.e: Pluto became a dwarf planet in 2006.

items.q: Why does the Sun look bigger and brighter than other stars?
c: It is much closer to Earth.
It is the biggest star in the universe.
items.e: Distance changes how bright a star looks.

items.q: What is a galaxy?
c: a huge group of billions of stars, gas and dust
items.e: We live in the Milky Way.

items.q: Gravity on the Moon is about 1/6 as strong as on Earth. A rover weighs 240 newtons on Earth. About how much does it weigh on the Moon?
items.e: 240 ÷ 6 = 40 newtons. The amount of matter is the same, but the Moon's weaker gravity pulls less.

items.q: Which quantity stays the same on the Moon as on the Earth: mass or weight?
items.e: Mass (kg) stays the same; weight (N) depends on gravity.

items.q: What is the habagat?
c: the southwest monsoon, a warm, moist wind that brings heavy rain
items.e: It blows from about June to September.

items.q: On Venus (g = 8.9 N/kg), Rose's backpack weighs 17.8 N. What is its mass?
items.e: mass = weight ÷ g = 17.8 ÷ 8.9 = 2 kg.

items.q: The Moon orbits at a radius of 384,400 km and takes 27.3 days per orbit. What is its average orbital speed? (v = 2πr ÷ T)
What are the two seasons in the Philippines?
c: the dry season and the wet (rainy) season
a cold season and a hot season
a windy season and a calm season
items.e: PAGASA divides the year into dry and wet seasons.

items.q: A newly found object orbits the Sun with an average distance of 0.25 AU. Using T² = a³, what is its orbital period?

Gravitational field strength on the Moon is 1.6 N/kg. What is the weight there of an object with a mass of 10 kg?
items.e: weight = mass × g = 10 × 1.6 = 16 N.

items.q: Why is the Philippines warm all year?
c: it is in the tropics, close to the equator
it is high above the clouds
it is in the polar region
it has more Moon than Sun
items.e: Sunlight hits the tropics almost straight down.

items.q: Gravitational field strength on Venus is 8.9 N/kg. What is the weight there of an object with a mass of 70 kg?
items.e: weight = mass × g = 70 × 8.9 = 623 N.

items.q: Earth around the Sun orbits at a radius of 150,000,000 km and takes 365.25 days per orbit. What is its average orbital speed? (v = 2πr ÷ T)
A newly found object orbits the Sun with an average distance of 25 AU. Using T² = a³, what is its orbital period?
Which months are usually the hottest in the Philippines?
items.e: The hot dry season is from March to May.

items.q: Why is the Philippines warm even in December?
c: it is far from the ocean
it is near the North Pole
it is near the equator and receives strong sunlight all year
items.e: Places in the tropics are warm all year.

items.q: A comet takes 0.008 years to orbit the Sun. Using T² = a³, what is its average distance from the Sun?
When is the rainy season in most of the Philippines?
c: the whole year with no change
items.e: The southwest monsoon brings rain.

items.q: What is the amihan?
c: the northeast monsoon, a cooler, drier wind from about November to February
items.e: Amihan brings cooler weather to Luzon.

items.q: On the Moon (g = 1.6 N/kg), Nico's backpack weighs 80 N. What is its mass?
items.e: mass = weight ÷ g = 80 ÷ 1.6 = 50 kg.

items.q: What is weight?
c: the force of gravity on an object
the amount of matter in an object
items.e: Mass (kg) stays the same; weight (N) depends on gravity.

items.q: What is mass?
c: the force of gravity on it
the amount of matter in an object
items.e: Mass (kg) stays the same; weight (N) depends on gravity.

items.q: Rose puts plastic wrap over a bowl of water in the sun with a cold cup on top. Drops form under the wrap. What two processes does this model show?
items.e: Water evaporates, then condenses on the cool plastic.

items.q: What is runoff?
c: water that flows over the land into streams and lakes
items.e: Runoff can carry pollution.

items.q: Why do puddles dry faster on hot, sunny days?
c: Gravity is stronger on hot days.
More energy from the sun makes water evaporate faster.
items.e: More thermal energy, faster evaporation.

items.q: Hazel uses 100 drops of water to model Earth's water. How many drops should she set aside for fresh water?
Why does the Earth's tilt matter for seasons?
c: the part tilted toward the Sun gets more direct sunlight and longer days
the tilted part is closer to the Moon
items.e: Direct sunlight heats the surface more.

items.q: What should people prepare for in the rainy season?
items.e: Clean drains and prepare go bags.

items.q: Patricia's class is studying precipitation. What mainly drives this part of the water cycle?
items.e: Energy from the sun drives evaporation and transpiration; gravity pulls water down as precipitation and runoff; cooling causes condensation.

items.q: Water expands by about 9% when it freezes. 300 mL of water freezes in a rock crack. About what volume does the ice take up?
Which statement about El Niño is correct?
c: it can bring less rain and drought to the Philippines
it makes the Earth stop rotating
items.e: During El Niño, rain is often below normal.

items.q: If glaciers melt into the ocean, what happens to that fresh water?
c: It becomes part of the salty ocean.
items.e: Melting ice that flows into the ocean mixes with salt water.

items.q: Which statement about La Niña is correct?
c: it can bring more rain and stronger storms to the Philippines
items.e: La Niña is the opposite of El Niño.

Baguio is high in the mountains, where air is cooler
items.e: Temperature drops as altitude increases.

items.q: Trisha weighs a potted plant in a sealed bag for 3 days. The bag gets foggy. What process caused this?
items.e: Plants release water vapor from their leaves.

items.q: How should farmers use the rainy season?
c: they plant rice and other crops that need a lot of water

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the waxing gibbous?
items.e: New → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → last quarter → waning crescent.

items.q: Earth turns 360° in 24 hours. How many degrees does it turn in 12 hours?
Tonight Camille sees a third quarter. Which phase came just before it?
items.e: The cycle is new → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → third quarter → waning crescent, about 29.5 days.

items.q: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
items.e: That is why we have years.

items.q: What happens in a solar eclipse?
c: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks the Sun.
items.e: Never look at the Sun, even during an eclipse.

items.q: Tonight Ramon sees a full moon. Which phase came just before it?
items.e: The cycle is new → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → third quarter → waning crescent, about 29.5 days.

items.q: Why are shadows shortest at noon?
c: It is always cloudy at noon.
The Sun is highest in the sky.
The Sun is lowest in the sky.
items.e: High Sun, short shadow.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the waxing crescent?
items.e: New → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → last quarter → waning crescent.

items.q: Stars seem to move about 15° across the sky each hour because Earth spins. Bryan watches a star for 8 hours. About how many degrees does it move?
Nico sketches the Moon from the Northern Hemisphere. Which phase is shown?
items.e: Waxing phases are lit on the right; waning phases are lit on the left.

items.q: What causes day and night?
items.e: One rotation takes about 24 hours.

items.q: The Earth turns 15° every hour. How long does it take to turn 90°?

items.e: Waxing phases are lit on the right; waning phases are lit on the left.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the first quarter?
items.e: New → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → last quarter → waning crescent.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the waxing gibbous?
items.e: Waxing means growing; waning means shrinking.

items.q: Tonight Kristine sees a waxing gibbous. About which phase will Kristine see one week later?
items.e: The cycle is new → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → third quarter → waning crescent, about 29.5 days.

items.q: How long does the Earth take to spin round once?
items.e: Day and night happen because the Earth spins; the Sun only seems to move.

items.q: When it is day for us, which way is our side of the Earth facing?
items.e: Day and night happen because the Earth spins; the Sun only seems to move.

items.q: Why do we see the same side of the Moon all the time?
c: The Moon spins once for each orbit of Earth.
The other side is dark forever.
items.e: This is called being tidally locked.
